detail:
The National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NHLBI) describes asthma as a chronic, long-term condition that affects the airways in the lungs. In asthma, the airways can become inflamed and narrowed at times, which makes it harder for air to flow out when breathing. NHLBI notes that asthma affects about 1 in 13 people in the United States, affects people of all ages, and often starts during childhood.

Symptoms can include wheezing, coughing, shortness of breath, and chest tightness, and patterns described in the sources include symptoms that come and go and worsen with triggers such as pollen, exercise, viral infections, or cold air. When symptoms worsen sharply, sources call the episode an asthma attack or flare-up. Clinicians usually diagnose asthma from medical history and a physical exam together with lung function tests such as spirometry, and sometimes allergy testing or other tests. NHLBI states that there is no cure for asthma, and that treatment and an asthma action plan are the established ways the condition is managed.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about asthma symptoms and testing.

title: Asthma: when inflamed airways narrow and breathing gets harder
